title: Grade 8 French — Fri, Jun 20
description: Le futur simple — Day 5 of 5: Week review + mixed practice
subject: french

questions.question: Conjugate 'finir' in the futur simple for all six persons: je/tu/il/nous/vous/ils.
Identify the verb and tense: 'Nous serons en vacances dans deux semaines.'
questions.explanation: serons = ser- (être futur stem) + -ons = futur simple. 'We will be on vacation in two weeks.'

questions.question: Fill in with the correct futur simple form: 'Qu'est-ce que tu _____ (faire) ce week-end?'
questions.explanation: faire → fer- + -as = tu feras. 'What will you do this weekend?'

questions.question: Translate into French using futur simple: 'They will come to the party.' (venir)
options: Ils sont venus à la fête.
questions.explanation: venir → viendr- + -ont = ils viendront. 'Ils viendront à la fête.'

questions.question: Which sentence contains an error?
options: Tu auras besoin d'un parapluie demain.
Nous ferons nos devoirs ce soir.
questions.explanation: 'serat' does not exist. être futur: ser- + -a = elle sera. The error is the extra -t; correct form is 'elle sera'.

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'Si j'étais riche, j'achèterais une grande maison.'
options: étais = imperfect (si clause), achèterais = conditionnel (result clause)
questions.explanation: Classic 'si + imperfect → conditionnel' structure. étais = imperfect; achèterais = conditionnel (would buy). This is a hypothetical.

questions.question: Complete: 'Bientôt, les élèves _____ leurs examens.' (passer = to take an exam)
questions.explanation: 'Bientôt' (soon) = future signal → futur simple. passer + -ont = ils passeront. 'Soon, the students will take their exams.'

questions.question: For the -re verb 'entendre' (to hear), the futur simple je-form is:
questions.explanation: entendre → drop -e → entendr- + -ai = j'entendrai. Common error: keeping the -e (*j'entenderai).

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'Vous _____ (avoir) les résultats la semaine prochaine.'
questions.explanation: 'La semaine prochaine' (next week) = definite future → futur simple. aur- + -ez = vous aurez.

questions.question: Translate: 'Tomorrow, we will go to the market and we will buy vegetables.' (aller, acheter)
options: Demain, nous allons au marché et nous achetons des légumes.
Demain, nous irons au marché et nous achèterons des légumes.
Demain, nous allions au marché et nous achetions des légumes.
Demain, nous sommes allés au marché et avons acheté.
questions.explanation: aller → ir- + -ons = nous irons. acheter → achèter- + -ons = nous achèterons. Both futur simple.

questions.question: Which irregular futur stem is WRONG?
questions.explanation: aller → futur stem is ir- (not all-). So j'irai, tu iras, il ira, nous irons, vous irez, ils iront.

questions.question: Change to futur simple: 'Il fait beau aujourd'hui.' (It is nice weather today.)
questions.explanation: faire → fer- + -a = il fera. 'Il fera beau demain.' = It will be nice (weather) tomorrow.

questions.question: Mixed practice: 'Dans 10 ans, je _____ médecin.' (être)
questions.explanation: 'Dans 10 ans' (in 10 years) = future → futur simple. ser- + -ai = je serai. 'In 10 years, I will be a doctor.'

questions.question: Read this mini-paragraph and identify all futur simple verbs: 'Ce soir, je finirai mes devoirs. Ensuite, je regarderai un film. Demain, nous irons au parc.'
options: finirai ✓, regarderai ✓, irons ✓ — all futur simple
finirai = futur, regarderai = conditionnel, irons = présent
finirai = futur, other two are imperfect
questions.explanation: finirai (finir + -ai), regarderai (regarder + -ai), irons (ir- + -ons) — all three are futur simple forms.

questions.question: Final summary: What is the one key rule that applies to ALL futur simple conjugations, regular AND irregular?
options: Always use the present tense stem + endings
Always use the FUTUR STEM (infinitive for regular verbs; special stem for irregular) + endings -ai/-as/-a/-ons/-ez/-ont
Always use the imperfect stem + future endings
Use the past participle + avoir/être conjugated in future
questions.explanation: The universal rule: futur simple = STEM + -ai/-as/-a/-ons/-ez/-ont. For regular verbs, stem = infinitive (-er/-ir verbs) or infinitive minus -e (-re verbs). For irregular verbs (être/avoir/aller/faire/venir), use the special stem.
